title: Review of c31's crawlers from noise (SIBM): cells, rings and self-polarized crawling replicate on fresh seed 7, and the linear-kinetics twin dies static; but no track reaches 3 body lengths on this seed (labkit max 2.0; the final large crawler 1.5-2.2 unwrapped)
summary: Re-ran world.py unchanged on fresh seed 7 (labkit, 80 frames, t=16) and with KIN=1 on the same seed. From the thresholded random field (t=0), round cells form by t~0.6, the larger ones polarize by t~1.4-2 and crawl as half-moons, crawlers absorb static disks, and by t~6 one large crawler remains with two small static disks (rerun/sheet.png, rerun/tracks.png #35, #31). Layer: s rim/core 4.2, rim/outside 12, 12/17 individuals membrane-like. Motion: labkit 2 long-lived tracks >= 1 body length, max 2.0; following the largest body by overlap with periodic unwrapping (bigpath.py), it moves 276 px = 2.2 body lengths from t=4 to 16 and 1.5 from t=8 to 16 (bigpath.txt). KIN=1 twin: all bodies vanish by t~8, max 0.2 body lengths.

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0: random two-phase field over the whole box
observations.I: rerun/tracks.png #2 and #29: round cells hold their shape from t~0.6 to the end
observations.B: rerun/radial.png: s rim/core 4.2, rim/out 12, 12/17 individuals; source kp*phi*rho is the cell's own bound protein

seeds_run.result: partial: cells, layer and self-polarized crawling reproduce; motion stays below 3 body lengths (labkit 2.0, largest crawler 2.2 unwrapped); KIN=1 twin static and extinct

controls_run.M: rerun_linear (KIN=1, seed 7): no motion, all bodies gone by t~8

verdicts.limitation: M is not shown at the 3-body-length gate on seed 7: crawlers merge into one large cell that is slow per body length (sqrt area 125-128 px), and each merge breaks labkit tracks; the run is short (t=16). The claim's own seeds give 1.4-3.6, so M rests on seed 1's 3.6. The s layer is a quasi-equilibrium coating pushed by a drift written against phi; it counts because the cell's protein makes all of it. The cyt cap (2.5) is a regularization I did not test.
